etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English delare, from Old English dǣlere, from Proto-West Germanic [Term?]. By surface analysis, deal +‎ -er. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Deeler, West Frisian dieler, Dutch deler, German Teiler, Swedish delare.

definitions.definition: One who deals in goods, especially automobiles; a middleman.
A drug dealer, one who peddles illicit drugs.

quote.citation: 1967, Leonard Cohen (lyrics and music), “The Stranger Song”, in Songs of Leonard Cohen:
quote.text: It's true that all the men you knew were dealers  Who said they were through with dealing

definitions.definition: A particular type of stock broker or trader.
The person who deals the cards in a card game.
One who deals or metes out anything.

quote.citation: 2018, Kate Stanley, Practices of Surprise in American Literature after Emerson, page 90:
quote.text: Dealt a decisive blow, Newman himself becomes a vengeful dealer of blows, perpetuating the repetitive cycle of repression and eruption  […]
